question.text: Under the page 36 hedging-versus-insurance distinction, which derivative products lock in a known fixed future return?

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 36 of the NISM Series-I workbook draws a hedging-versus-insurance distinction: hedging locks in a known future return by fixing the price (forwards and futures), while insurance via options pays a premium to selectively remove downside while keeping upside open. The Trap: The broader workbook elsewhere uses "hedging" more loosely: page 46 says currency risks can be hedged through forwards, futures, swaps and options, page 68 says options can be used for hedging, and page 96 lists futures and options as hedge choices. Under the narrower page 36 distinction used in this stem, only forwards and futures lock in a fixed return. Note: Source pages checked: 36, 46, 68 and 96 of the NISM Series-I workbook.
